children: A local judge rejected an injunction aimed at invalidating the licenses for the construction of Silvercorp Metals'
El Domo polymetallic project, which is expected to be Ecuador's third industrial mine, BNAmericas.com reported Thursday.
scored the legal victory over local non-governmental organization CEDHU, which filed the measure alleging the project violates human rights.
Following testing and adjustments, the $300M project is expected to start producing copper and other metals in H2 2027 and to reach capacity in 2028, Silvercorp
El Domo's environmental license was obtained in January 2024, and the company has said the project's environmental impact study had the support of 98% of residents.
Construction of El Domo began in early 2025, with commercial production targeted for mid-to-July 2027 at ~1,850 tons/day and an expected mine life of 11.5-13 years.

title: Silvercorp's El Domo mine in Ecuador to start operations next year after legal win
